translations.source_sense_description: Technik

glosses: Living or taking place in the air.

examples.text: The seabirds put on an astonishing aerial display.

glosses: Made up of air or gas; gaseous.

examples.text: A soul [...] was first conceived to be an aerial, or an igneous substance, which animates the body during life, and makes its escape at death [...].

glosses: Positioned high up; elevated.

examples.text: The aerial photographs clearly showed the damage caused by the storm.

glosses: Ethereal, insubstantial; imaginary.

examples.text: the great Recompence in view, for which the most exalted Minds have with so much Alacrity, sacrifis'd their Quiet, Health, sensual Pleasures, and every inch of themselves, has never been any thing else but the Breath of Man, the Aerial Coyn of Praise.

glosses: Pertaining to the air or atmosphere; atmospheric.
Pertaining to a vehicle which travels through the air; airborne; relating to or conducted by means of aircraft.

examples.text: aerial photography
an aerial view of the landscape

In his submission to the UN, [Christof] Heyns points to the experience of drones. Unmanned aerial vehicles were intended initially only for surveillance, and their use for offensive purposes was prohibited, yet once strategists realised their perceived advantages as a means of carrying out targeted killings, all objections were swept out of the way.

glosses: Above the ground
A rod, wire, or other structure for receiving or transmitting radio, television signals etc.
A move, as in dancing or skateboarding, involving one or both feet leaving the ground.

examples.text: In their dancing, clubbers were flamboyant. They experimented with new dance steps and improvisations, including risky maneuvers and aerials in which women were flipped into the air.

glosses: A move that involves performing a full rotation while in the air, without touching any equipment such as a balance beam or panel mat with one's hands.
An aerial photograph.

examples.text: Hemment is on record as being the first person to film aerials of wildlife – he filmed a flock of wild ducks early in 1911, possibly on Rainey's Louisiana property.

glosses: A highly-contrasting visual artifact in the form of a band or ring.

examples.text: Lanczos3 for sharp results. May produce aerials. — Krita 5.2.2

translations.source_sense_description: Technik

glosses: Longue vergue qui s’attache obliquement au mât, pour soutenir une voile triangulaire.

examples.text: L’antenne tient lieu de la vergue dans les voiles latines, mais il est beaucoup moins dangereux de se tenir sur les vergues, car elles sont toujours dans une position horizontale.
Le gros bout d'une antenne s'appelle carnal : c'est où est frappé l’oste , ou c'est aussi l’empointure inférieure de la voile.

Et les vents alizés inclinaient leurs antennes
Aux bords mystérieux du monde Occidental.

glosses: Élément secondaire d'un ensemble quelconque qui dérive de la structure principale et qui y reste liée.

examples.text: Au moment de l'armistice, le raccordement avec la voie normale à Saint-Hilaire était posé; celui d’Autry était en cours d'exécution. Les antennes de pénétration s'arrêtaient respectivement à Quilly (3 kilomètres au sud de Coulommes-et-Marqueny) et à Pauvres, celle de Tugny n'était pas commencée.

glosses: Rang de futailles placées les unes sur les autres dans la cale.
Appendice articulé en forme de corne, que les insectes portent sur la tête, et que l’on croit être pour eux l’organe principal du tact.

examples.text: L’antenne de ce Leptodactyle se compose de dix articles bien comptés. Le premier, ou l'article basilaire qui forme le pédicule de toute l’antenne, est corroïde et d'une conformation ordinaire.
On peut même couper avec des ciseaux les deux antennes d'un Zygène sans troubler son repas, bien qu'une goutte de sang jaune vienne perler sur la surface de section.

glosses: Ce qui permet aux personnes de percevoir intuitivement ou intellectuellement leur environnement.

examples.text: Pas davantage n'avait-il pu acquérir les antennes, indispensables aux politiques, dont la pratique des affaires pourvoit d'aventure ceux auquel la nature, en les dotant d'intelligence, a refusé l'intuition.

Ces gens-là, on le sait, possèdent de redoutables antennes : incapables d’éprouver certains sentiments, ils les détectent infailliblement chez les autres, lors même que ceux-ci n’en sont pas encore avertis.

glosses: Appareillage métallique passif isolé de la terre et relié à des appareils de radiocommunication, destiné à émettre ou recevoir des ondes radio.

examples.text: Tous les bras disponibles travaillaient à la confection d’un mât, auquel les électriciens du Vaterland accrocheraient les longues antennes de l’appareil de télégraphie sans fil qui devait enfin relier le Prince au monde extérieur.

Les antennes de l'appareil étaient toutes secouées, dans la nuit, d'une vibration puissante, et le récepteur enregistrait à mesure les mots d'une dépêche en langue espagnole lancée par la station de Nauen.

glosses: Chaîne de radio ou de télévision.

examples.text: Critiqués sur l'antenne de RMC par Jérôme Rothen et Jean-Michel Larqué pour les tenues arborées en arrivant à Clairefontaine, les Bleus ont été défendus par Jules Koundé.

Plus de nos jours... Ne rien cacher tout étaler... Nous c'est l'ère du bikinisme, de l’àpoilisme. Ni dissimulation ni tricherie, tout sur les antennes, les écrans et les ondes, capté par les populations.

glosses: Implantation locale d’une organisation.

examples.text: L’antenne de la mairie est dans la troisième rue à gauche

glosses: Someone or something that feels.

examples.text: Are you more of a feeler or more of a thinker?

glosses: An antenna or appendage used for feeling, especially on an insect.
Something ventured to test another's feelings, opinion, or position.

examples.text: I sent out some feelers but they didn't seem interested.
This survey is designed to get a feeler about how the citizens feel about the proposed new highway.
In 1905, the Russo-Japanese war fought itself to a standstill, and with the destruction of Rozhiestvensky's fleet at Tsushima, the Japanese, for financial reasons, had to put out feelers for peace.

Mr. Dayan's peace feeler would he more attractive to Cairo if it were accompanied by suggestions from Jerusalem, public private, for safeguarding Israeli security interests there without sacrificing Cairo's claim to ultimate sovereignty.

glosses: a presumptive person; someone who bases on gut feeling, such as assuming or imagining that something said or done, whether positive or negative, was for a person despite having no concrete confirmation but gut feeling, or someone who assumes one's affection is reciprocated, or indulges in one's own wishful thinking or flatters oneself

translations.source_sense_description: Zoologie: Sinnesorgan einiger Gliederfüßer zum Erfassen der Umwelt

glosses: An appendage used for sensing on the head of an insect, crab, or other animal.

examples.text: The overall shape of most insect antennae is elongate and cylindrical, although elaborations into plumose, lamellate, or pectinate forms have arisen many times in different insect lineages.

He put his fingers over his head like two antennas, crossed his eyes, and waggled his tongue like some kind of insect.
In the same work, Brown uses antennae to refer to both aerials and feelers during more technical descriptions.
The basis of these relationships lies in the olfactory chemoreceptors of insect antennas...

glosses: An apparatus to receive or transmit electromagnetic waves and convert respectively to or from an electrical signal.
The faculty of intuitive astuteness.

examples.text: Most nurses believe they are born with an antenna of sorts, which is able to guide them through clinical practice and help them determine what is right and what is not...
Obama is astute. He approaches things with the help of a sensitive antenna.

glosses: A fragment of an oligosaccharide
The spar to which a lateen sail is attached, which is then hoisted up the mast.

examples.text: Despite the rough voice, the coach is surprisingly feeling.

examples.text: He made a feeling representation of his wrongs.

examples.text: The wool on my arm produced a strange feeling.

glosses: Emotion; impression.

examples.text: The house gave me a feeling of dread.
Part of the 'western arcade' (as it's known) is lined with delis, cafes and other shops, giving it the feeling of a bazaar.

glosses: Emotional state or well-being.

examples.text: You really hurt my feelings when you said that.

glosses: Emotional attraction or desire.

examples.text: Many people still have feelings for their first love.

You can kiss a hundred boys in bars
Shoot another shot, try to stop the feeling
You can say it's just the way you are
Make a new excuse, another stupid reason

glosses: Intuition.

examples.text: He has no feeling for what he can say to somebody in such a fragile emotional condition.
I've got a funny feeling that this isn't going to work.
Got on a lucky one / Came in eighteen to one / I've got a feeling / This year's for me and you

glosses: An opinion, an attitude.

examples.text: When you are tempted to speculate in cocoa, lie down until the feeling goes away.
